body.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
k_n\uparrow\infty,\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,\qquad
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{loc},n}&& (r\in\mathcal L_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{shell},n}&& (r\in\mathcal X_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{zero},n}&& (r\in\mathcal Z_n).
\end{aligned} \tag{A}
\]
The same output contains a total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) satisfying
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\left[\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-
\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le n^{-1}-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}. \tag{B}
\]
It also outputs a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) such that \(E(N)\to0\) and, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N). \tag{C}
\]
The inequalities (A)--(C), including exterior and zero-count control, are theorem conclusions and are not inputs or assumptions.  They imply the finite certified squeeze
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]
body.justification: The root theorem is retained as the exact corrected-prior all-count bridge that would convert the finite experiment into the sharp unrestricted second-order value.
body.gap: The compact rational Airy approximation and exact finite evaluator do not imply uniform local, exterior-shell, or zero-face posterior-risk bounds; these must be derived with an effective common error sequence.
body.consumer: A prospective unequal three-regimen binary-endpoint design may use the proved fixed-design benchmark and same-input intervals now; the unrestricted sharp benchmark awaits this theorem.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the lower-bound parts of conclusions (A)--(C) of the corrected target: one design-independent corrected Airy-tube diagonal must bound the fixed-count Bayes deficit uniformly on the \(n^{-1/6}\) local allocation face, every positive-count exterior allocation, and every zero-count face, and these three errors must admit one computable monotone tail majorant tending to zero.
obligation.obstruction: The exact evaluator only computes each finite Bayes maximum. Neither the frozen core nor the presolve supplies a target-specific Bayes-information identity or a likelihood expansion with a remainder uniform in allocation counts, spline index, transverse width, rare response types, posterior denominators, and boundary faces. Finite enumeration at each \(n\) cannot certify a statement for every future sample size. Assuming those bounds or the tail majorant would assume the theorem's crux. The primal error is not part of the obstruction: the rational-grid lemma gives it an explicit vanishing bound.
obligation.attempted: The widening polynomial prior was refuted by an exact Horvitz--Thompson Bayes-risk calculation. The longitudinal family was replaced by an effective rational spline-square approximation with a normalized-energy certificate; prior positivity, the exact finite-population target, permutation-orbit reduction, posterior square completion, and all finite allocation-stratum maxima were verified at every fixed admissible input. Randomized barycentric rounding of the established Airy estimator proves the matching total rational primal error is at most \((B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\). These steps do not control the cross-sample posterior quotient, especially when allocation counts approach zero.
obligation.partial_result: The effective normalized Airy-record lemma proves a uniform algorithm \(k\mapsto(T_k^\dagger,\varphi_k^\dagger,w_k^\dagger,\text{record})\), using only rational interval ODE/Taylor calculations and certified weighted tails.  For each fixed admissible \((n,k,\varepsilon,\delta)\), the corrected finite-input evaluator terminates, computes the exact ordered-field Bayes certificate and all three allocation-stratum maxima, and returns a total rational finite procedure.  The permutation-orbit lemma gives \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\).  Randomized barycentric rounding and the established fixed-design theorem give the independently proved attaining coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) with the effective primal error bound \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\le(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\).  What remains is cross-sample, design-uniform control of the three computed Bayes lower-bound errors.
